title: Data, Secrets & Identity: Who Can Access What?
subtitle: Separate database permissions, network access, task startup permissions and application identity.
analogy: An execution role is the stage crew that fetches the image and startup secrets. A task role is the badge worn by running application code. Database users are a separate permission system.
objectives: Explain transactions, database schemas and connection limits.
Keep database/cache endpoints private and encrypt connections.
Distinguish execution roles, task roles and EC2 instance profiles.
Inject a managed secret without writing its value into source or Terraform state.
prerequisites: Network/subnet IDs and security groups from Chapter 3 for the manual path.
Or read this chapter as preparation and build the complete stack with Terraform in Chapter 8.

lessons.title: PostgreSQL is the source of completed results
body: The job_id primary key identifies a result; a transaction groups database writes into a commit or rollback. The API reads completed results, while the queue tracks pending work. A database is not automatically a queue, and Redis is not the durable record of completed jobs.
Connection limits matter: each API process has its own pool. Count the maximum pooled connections plus workers, migrations and administrative sessions before increasing task count.

lessons.title: Secrets are values, not strings in Git
body: Use an RDS-managed master password in Secrets Manager. The ECS execution role reads the secret at startup and injects only the password JSON key as DB_PASSWORD. DB_HOST, DB_NAME and DB_USER are ordinary non-secret configuration.

Injected environment values are a snapshot. Secret rotation does not modify an already running process; deploy replacement tasks with current values. Do not print all environment variables while debugging.

lessons.title: The three AWS identities
body: The execution role permits image pulls, logs and startup secret retrieval. The task role grants runtime AWS API permissions; our text-processing task needs no S3 permissions. An optional EC2 instance profile lets the host register with ECS and use Systems Manager.

IAM does not open a network route. A correct role can still fail if private subnets cannot reach ECR, Secrets Manager or CloudWatch. KMS permissions are separate when you choose customer-managed encryption keys.

lessons.title: Lab versus production data access
body: The runnable lab uses the database owner for brevity and a single TLS-enabled Valkey node. A production app should use a restricted SQL role, certificate verification, cache authentication/ACLs, backups and failover.

DB_SSLMODE=require encrypts the RDS connection but does not provide the identity verification of verify-full. For verify-full, bundle the current RDS CA and set the driver’s root-certificate option. Local Compose intentionally uses unencrypted loopback-bound services.

handHoldingSteps: Manual path: create an RDS PostgreSQL 17 instance, DB appdb, owner appuser, private subnet group and data-sg. Choose managed master credentials in Secrets Manager and no public access. Record the endpoint and secret ARN; do not copy the secret into a committed file.
Create a private Redis-compatible Valkey replication group with in-transit encryption and data-sg. A single node is enough for this lab; use rediss://ENDPOINT:6379/0 for the application.

Create the execution role trusted by ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com with AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy and a secret retrieval policy scoped to your DB secret ARN. For a customer-managed KMS key, grant decrypt on that key separately.
Create a task role trusted by ECS tasks. Grant only the four ssmmessages channel actions if you plan to use ECS Exec; there is no need to grant S3 access to an app that never calls S3.
Use the task-definition fragment below as a reference when entering environment and secret fields in the next chapter. Replace every ARN/endpoint placeholder.
concepts: Three permission planes: Network groups permit TCP, IAM permits AWS APIs, and SQL roles permit database operations.
Secret injection: ECS startup reads Secrets Manager under the execution role, not the application task role.
TLS: rediss selects encrypted Redis transport; database require and verify-full provide different security guarantees.

architectureDescription: At task startup, the execution role reads the managed secret and injects a password. The application then uses database credentials over a private TLS connection; IAM and SQL permissions remain separate.

breakItDrill.title: Revoke secret retrieval
breakItDrill.scenario: Temporarily remove GetSecretValue from the manual execution role, then start a new task.
breakItDrill.symptom: The task stops before application startup with a secret initialization error.
breakItDrill.fix: Restore the scoped execution-role permission and start a new task; broadening the task role will not fix this startup failure.

assignment.title: Explain a startup failure
assignment.description: Write a short runbook distinguishing AccessDenied on secret retrieval, a network timeout to the database, and a SQL authentication failure.
assignment.completionHint: Verify the result yourself, then complete the chapter checklist.

recallNote.keyTakeaway: A secret reference can live in code; its plaintext value should not.
bullets: Execution role: pull/log/inject. Task role: application AWS APIs.
IAM, security groups and SQL users are separate controls.
Changing a secret requires an explicit refresh/deployment strategy.
